lead.headline: Game shelves carry the home-computer pitch
lead.dek: As March 1983 begins, Computer Gaming World keeps strategy, adventure, and simulation titles in view while retailers use games to make home machines feel useful and fun.
lead.body: During the week of February 28-March 6, 1983, the home-computer market was still being explained from the shelf outward. Computer Gaming World's early-1983 issues put titles such as Serpentine, Cosmic Balance, S.E.U.I.S., Armor Assault, and wider strategy coverage in front of readers who wanted more than arcade imitation. At the same time, IBM PC shoppers were hearing the new Lotus 1-2-3 pitch, a spreadsheet/database/graphics package that had gone on sale in January and was quickly becoming a reason to take the PC seriously at work.
